idiom_name: frozen object literal (Symbol or string values) + boundary parser
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no enum construct, so the accepted idiom is an object literal frozen with Object.freeze: Symbol values give identity and cannot collide with strings, string values are serializable but compare equal to raw strings. A class with static readonly fields and private construction is the closest approach to instance control. None of this is enforced by a compiler - there is no type system to make the set closed - so validation at the boundary plus freeze is the whole guarantee; prefer TypeScript when the guarantee must be checked.
pitfalls: Object.freeze is shallow: nested metadata objects remain mutable unless deep-frozen.
Symbol values disappear from JSON (JSON.stringify emits undefined) and Symbol.for registrations are global and shared across realms.
String-valued members still compare equal to raw strings, so a typo can pass an equality check while a misspelled property lookup yields undefined only later.
